Assessment

Executive summary

The brand is distinctive and memorable. The largest conversion gains should come from shortening the path to products, making shipping and return costs explicit at the decision point, and removing avoidable cart friction.

Bottom line The brand is distinctive and memorable. The largest conversion gains should come from shortening the path to products, making shipping and return costs explicit at the decision point, and removing avoidable cart friction.

What is already working

  • Strong Southern-Western visual identity and distinctive photography.
  • Clear product pricing and useful predictive search once a query is entered.
  • Broad category coverage supported by quick-view and add-to-cart actions.
  • Credible family-owned story, physical store locations, and multiple payment methods.

Findings

Seven findings with evidence

Open each finding for observed friction, recommended treatment and screenshots. Click any screenshot to enlarge it. Mark findings as reviewed as your team works through them; progress is saved in this browser.

Observed friction

  • The hero communicates the brand clearly but delays product and category discovery.
  • “Most Items Ship Free” is less precise than the policy, which requires eligible orders over $75 and excludes items such as hats and boots.
  • “Shop” and “Collections” create a classification choice before visitors understand the difference.
  • The homepage “SHOP SALES” CTA routes back to the homepage instead of a sale collection.

Recommended treatment

  • Reduce the hero height enough to reveal category shortcuts or a product row.
  • Use one shipping statement everywhere: “Free shipping on eligible orders $75+.”
  • Expose five or six high-intent category links immediately below the hero.
  • Audit all promotional CTAs whenever homepage campaigns change.
Conversion risk Visitors who clicked New Arrivals have already expressed shopping intent. Requiring additional scrolling before showing products adds friction at the highest-intent moment.

Recommended treatment

  • Limit collection campaign imagery to approximately 250–350px on desktop and less on mobile.
  • Reduce the introduction to one or two lines with an optional “Read more.”
  • Show product count, active filter chips and the first product row in the first viewport.
  • Add category chips for Boots, Hats, Apparel, Jewelry, Bags and Gifts where relevant.

Observed friction

  • Visible blank image areas make the page feel unfinished and reduce confidence while browsing.
  • Available filters emphasize Availability, Price and Brand, while common shopping attributes are absent.
  • Product cards do not consistently show high-value badges such as New, Best Seller, Final Sale or USA Made.

Recommended treatment

  • Reserve image dimensions, use correctly sized WebP/AVIF assets and tune lazy-loading thresholds.
  • Add Product type, Size, Color, Material, Price and In-stock filters.
  • Display product count, selected filter chips and a clear reset action.
  • Use badges and variant cues to support faster comparison without opening every item.
Strength to build on Predictive results are useful once a query is entered. The opportunity is to make the empty state equally helpful and ensure thumbnails appear promptly.

Recommended treatment

  • Populate popular searches and high-intent category shortcuts.
  • Include recent searches for returning visitors where privacy settings permit.
  • Prioritize product thumbnails and reserve their dimensions to avoid blank placeholders.
  • Test common synonyms, misspellings and product attributes such as “cowgirl boots” and “turquoise earrings.”

Observed friction

  • A purchasable size is selected by default, increasing the risk of accidental variant orders.
  • The size guide is buried among gallery images rather than placed beside the size selector.
  • Shipping eligibility, delivery estimate and the $15 oversize return charge are absent from the purchase area.
  • No customer rating or review signal is visible near the title and price.

Recommended treatment

  • Start with “Select a size” and block Add to cart until the customer chooses.
  • Place measurement-based size guidance beside the selector.
  • Add three concise reassurance lines: estimated delivery, shipping eligibility and return terms.
  • Include rating, review count, stock status and a sticky mobile purchase bar.
  • Show the chosen size in the add-to-cart confirmation.

Observed friction

  • The standard navigation disappears, leaving no obvious “Continue shopping” route.
  • Checkout is disabled behind a mandatory checkbox, but the terms link routes to the homepage.
  • “Shipping calculated at checkout” delays a cost already partly defined by the oversize policy.
  • Payment and trust signals sit in the footer rather than next to checkout.

Recommended treatment

  • Restore a simplified header with logo, Continue shopping and secure-checkout language.
  • Fix the terms URL and remove the checkbox unless it is legally required.
  • Show accurate free-shipping progress only for eligible items; identify exclusions explicitly.
  • Place delivery expectations, payment options and returns reassurance beside checkout.

After-hours booking

  • Rename the navigation item to “After-Hours Events” or “Private Shopping.”
  • Use the form as the primary booking route and present email as a fallback.
  • Replace preselected Event Type, Party Size and Location values with neutral “Choose…” states.
  • State expected response time, available locations and typical availability near the form.

Shipping and returns

  • Rewrite the announcement to match the actual threshold and eligibility rules.
  • Add a clear return window, initiation instructions, refund timing and condition requirements.
  • Display product-specific charges before Add to cart rather than requiring policy-page research.

Ongoing

Accessibility corrections

  • Add a clear homepage H1 and correct heading hierarchy on the event page.
  • Replace generic labels such as “Button aria-label” with descriptive names.
  • Provide meaningful accessible labels for the logo, campaign links and carousel destinations.
  • Verify keyboard focus visibility, dialog focus trapping and text/background contrast at mobile and desktop breakpoints.

Performance priorities

  • Preload only the primary above-the-fold hero asset.
  • Serve responsive WebP/AVIF images sized to their rendered dimensions.
  • Reserve layout space for every image and use a branded low-resolution placeholder.
  • Defer nonessential gallery assets and third-party scripts until after the core shopping interface is interactive.
Validation This report is based on a live desktop review. Validate the same templates at key mobile widths before release, with special attention to sticky navigation, filters, gallery behavior and checkout controls.

Review method

The assessment followed the live customer path from landing and discovery through product evaluation and cart handoff. Screenshots document interface states observed on 25 August 2026. Recommendations are qualitative UX guidance and should be validated through analytics, usability testing and controlled experiments.

Important note

The cart contained one product solely to inspect the cart interface. No checkout, booking form or other transaction was submitted.
